g.text: The same cipher, four implementations on Windows on ARM: here the platform's own is the fast one

ISA-L is x86-64 assembly and has no ARM64 build, so its slot goes to a hand-written NEON implementation -- AESE/AESMC and PMULL through MSVC intrinsics, four blocks in flight, one reduction per four --

which answers the same question: what is there to win by doing the cipher ourselves? On x64 that was worth 55% over CNG; here it costs half. It is checked against CNG, OpenSSL and LibreSSL over a whole
32 KB packet, ciphertext and tag, before it is allowed to report a number. Nothing here throttles much: a virtual machine's clock is the host's business.
QEMU virtual machine, 4 vCPU, Windows 11 Pro 26200 ARM64 · the host processor is not visible from inside the guest, so read the rates against each other, not against a laptop
AES-128-GCM as SSH uses it: one complete GCM message per 32 KB packet, fresh IV, 4 bytes of AAD, 16-byte tag, one thread, no network
rsync 3.5.0 Windows port, github.com/nuket/rsync-windows · © 2026 Max Vilimpoc
